blocks.text: Speeches of Heads of State and Government, interventions to the United Nations and the League of Arab States, speeches for national holidays, inaugurations, election campaigns: the Arab rhetorical tradition is ancient and still alive, and a public speech in Arabic uses resources that institutional Italian uses less: parallelism, antithesis, repetition, prose rhyme, citation, titles of protocol. Knowing them serves to understand what the speech wants to achieve, to distinguish between what is promised and what is only evoked, and to translate without flattening or inflating the text. In this unit learn the main rhetorical figures and their Arabic names, protocol formulas, a method of analysis in five questions, and work on invented speeches and on a real public discourse chosen from institutional sources (Appendix C). The work is of linguistic analysis: no political judgement is required. Two weeks.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognising the parties to an official speech and the protocol formulas;
2. recognizing and naming in Arabic the main rhetorical figures (repection, parallelism, antithesis, question rhetoric, prose rhyme, quotation, metaphor, hyperbole, euphemism);
3. to distinguish in a speech the precise commitments from vague formulas, with the instruments of modality (B2-09);
4. translating a discourse by keeping the register and figures, without adding or removing emphasis;
5. write a short rhetorical analysis of a real public speech.
